content.thinking:
I should write the whole file carefully in one pass without verification, designing a qilin as a quadruped about 1.5 meters at the shoulder—deer/horse-like body with a dragon head, antlers, scaled hide, cloud-textured mane, flame-like fetlock tufts, an ox-tail-style fan tail with cloud curls, hooves, and gold accents.

I'm planning the cel shading and glowing details—eyes, forehead jewel, antler tips—then working out the skeleton: hips root, spine chain to chest, neck, head, jaw, tail chain, four IK legs, antlers, and ears, while being careful to use absolute model coordinates rather than local joint axes to avoid confusion. I'm sketching out approximate body proportions (shoulder height ~1.35m, total height with antlers ~2.3m) and placing the hip and spine joints using catmull-rom paths, then starting to lay out an arched neck toward the head position.

Now I'm adjusting the neck path so it connects seamlessly to the end of the spine chain, and I'm working through how to build the body as a lofted sweep connecting the tail root through hips to chest along the same spine path.

Placing hind legs around z≈-0.55 and forelegs near z≈0.35, with the body as a barrel-shaped ellipse radius (wider at chest) sitting around height 1.15. I'm defining spine path points from hips to shoulders and setting up a spine chain to drive a body sweep with that elliptical radius profile.

I continue the taper into a neck path rising from the chest base up to the head joint, with neck thickness narrowing from 0.17 to 0.1, and planning mane cards along the neck. Then I pause to check whether the spine chain's root joint is actually positioned at the origin.

Confirming the spine chain starts at the hips joint, I move to planning the tail: a path curving down from the hips through three tapering joints to a tip, with flame-wisp and cloud-curl card textures for the tuft. I'm now starting on the hind leg placement, setting the hip joint position before working out the leg's digitigrade structure.

For the hind leg, I'm computing a three-segment limb (thigh, shin, cannon) with bend directions, checking the reach distance against the hip-to-foot target, and setting the foot and hoof joint positions so the hoof frustum sits just above the ground, naming the joints hipHL, kneeHL, and hockHL.

For the hind leg I'm setting knee forward and hock back with the final segment vertical, checking lengths of 0.42/0.40/0.30 against a 0.9 reach for a slight bend. For the foreleg I'm placing the shoulder joint and target points, using elbow-back/knee-forward bends with segment lengths 0.36/0.38/0.3 against a reach near 1, giving subtle bending.

Now I'm working out leg thickness via a radius taper along each limb chain — thicker near the thigh (0.15) tapering down to the hoof (0.05) — then deciding on the color palette, leaning toward an ivory-white body with gold and jade scale accents for the qilin's classic look.

Building the scale pattern and fur-edge countershading...

Adding golden dorsal stripe logic...

Now I'm planning the head itself—a dragon-deer-lion hybrid with a skull joint aimed forward, a broad lion-like muzzle built from lofted stations, a hinged lower jaw, small tooth spikes, and long flowing dragon whiskers made from thin gold sweeps rigged to the head bone.

Continuing muzzle stations up to the upturned nose bulb with nostrils, then working out the lower jaw bone placement and loft stations below the muzzle.

Adding small fang spikes up from the jaw and down from the upper teeth, then working on eye placement as decals on the skull surface — figuring out position via azimuth/elevation, sizing, and choosing an amber-gold iris color that contrasts with the teal body, mirroring the decal for the opposite side.

Next I'm sketching brow ridges above the eyes, cheek frills as flat cards, and deer-like fin ears extruded in a leaf shape at the back-sides of the skull, angled outward.

Writing orthogonalization helper...

Now I'm planning the antlers as coral-like branching structures from the skull, with named joints for each antler base and a main beam that curves up and back via a sweep path, branching into several tines partway along.

Still planning antler colors...

For the forehead ornament, I'm positioning a glowing teal octahedron gem with a small gold frontlet shape extruded in front of it, plus a teardrop gold base behind. For the mane, I'm designing cloud-textured cards scattered along the neck sweep, using soft blue swirl shading with gold outlines for that cel-shaded cloud look.

Building the frame positions and tuft shapes...

Still writing SVG code...

I'll add simple crescent shading to each circle by layering slightly offset smaller circles for a bottom-right highlight effect, then plan two cloud texture variants—a tall wispy plume and a round swirled puff—and work out the mane placement along the neck using angle and count parameters.

I'm also considering extra tuft cards along the spine, forearms, and fetlocks, but deciding to skip floor-level cloud decorations since hooves need to rest at y=0. Instead I'll add small cloud curl anklets using a ring of cards around the fetlock on the leg chain.

For the fetlock flame tufts, I'm orienting the ring outward with cards leaning and flowing downward, sized around .14, using a teardrop flame texture in orange, gold, and cream tones to suggest fire.

For the tail, I'm scattering flame and cloud-plume cards along a sweep from mid-tail to tip at varying angles, with larger leaning cards near the end and a ring of long flame cards forming a feathered tuft at the very tip. I'm also considering adding dorsal scale details along the body.

Now I'm placing gold spikes along the spine using points sampled from the body sweep, oriented along the local axis, and sketching out cloven hooves as frustum-shaped cylinders positioned at each leg's foot joint.

I'm adding a thin gold trim ring around each hoof top for detail, skipping dewclaws for simplicity. Now I'm thinking about ornamentation like a golden collar with jade pendant and tassels around the qilin's neck, sweeping a closed loop around the neck joint's cross-section.

I need to pick the right point along the neck chain so the collar surface targets only the neck geometry and not the overlapping body, then plan a thicker gold collar band with hanging jade pendant spheres distributed along it.

For the pendant placement, I reason through the loop's angular convention: starting at the point closest to world up and going counterclockwise around the tangent direction, so the halfway point around the loop lands on the throat-facing underside — that's where I'll hang the gold-spiked jewel.

I'm positioning it with a small forward offset so it sits half-embedded at the collar surface rather than occluded inside the neck geometry, then considering adding a tassel hanging from the jewel using a small bezier tube or card frame.

Shifting to the rig now, I'm assigning roles across the skeleton—jaw and head hinges, spine/neck/tail chains, legs, and hinge roles for ears and eyelids—while keeping antlers and whiskers mostly rigid, though I'm weighing giving whiskers their own flexible chain similar to a tentacle role.

Deciding on two whisker chains, one per side with 3-4 joints each, swept with a tapering radius and parented to the head, curving outward and back from the muzzle in a wind-blown arc that clears the neck's mane geometry.

I'm skipping the end caps on the whiskers for simplicity, and adding a few scattered cloud-puff cheek tufts sprouting from the skull surface at symmetric angles for extra fur detail. For the skeleton hierarchy, I'm setting hips as root, with the spine chain parented to hips and the neck chain parented partway up the spine joints.

Then I'm wiring the head to parent off the final neck joint, the jaw off the head, the hind legs off the hips, and the front legs off the spine joint nearest the shoulder position based on where that joint's span falls along the body's z-axis.

For the legs, I'm checking how the limb helper works—taking Vector3 arrays and passing them into the chain builder with root, inner joints, and tip (four points, three spans, four names), optionally setting a ground contact point. I'm sketching out radius profiles for the hind leg sweep, tapering from a wide hip down to a narrower hock and foot, though the thigh blending near the hip still needs tuning.

I'm deciding to skip extra knee guard or cuff geometry and instead rely on painted bands, dropping the idea of a hock spur spike since the leg angle geometry is too ambiguous to place it cleanly. Now I'm shifting to defining the color palette and scale paint patterns—setting up jade and cream tones with scale textures for the back and belly.

Writing fur edge and shading logic...

Placing the gold cloud-swirl decal on the flank near the surface, with a mirrored version for the opposite side so the pattern flips symmetrically.

Writing spiral SVG path...

For the eye I'll use an amber iris color with default brow styling, and confirm the skull surface target works for hit detection. I'm considering whether to add shoulder pauldron-like plating to match the scaled, hooved chimera aesthetic but may skip underbelly trim to keep things simple.

For the chimera build I'm combining dragon head, deer antlers, ox tail, horse hooves, and lion mane flames, then adding flame wisp cards along the foreleg using a scatter filter targeting back-facing areas near the elbow.

I'm figuring out placement for pastern fire rings on each leg, working out chain position fractions to get the ring near the hoof at the correct height, then scattering flame cards around that ring.

Writing SVG flame paths...

Thinking through color choices now -- warm orange and gold flames against the teal body with jade belly and white-blue mane feels right for qilin fire lore. Then I move to the tail, setting up a sweep of frames along a curved path with varying radius and angle steps to build the tail cards.

I'm designing the tail as a graceful S-curve made of five joints with progressively narrower radii, with a cloud plume at the base and flame near the tip, then moving on to coding the mane frames.

Writing mane frame generation...

I'm realizing the standing-card approach has an issue: since cards face front and back but appear edge-on from the side, a mane viewed from the side could vanish entirely, so I need to adjust the lean angle so the card plane still reads as mane-like from most viewing angles.

Still working out flow directions...

For dorsal spikes, I'm placing twelve gold-colored spikes along the body surface between t=0.08 and 0.92, using the spike primitive with a base, tip direction, length and radius, with color passed through the options object.

Next I'm building the skull as a scaled sphere geometry placed near the head bone position, reusing the same coat material so the scale texture continues seamlessly from body onto head.

For the face details, I'm shading the belly region cream based on normal direction, giving the muzzle underside a lighter tone while adding a coral nose pad. I'm sweeping gold catmull-rom curves above the eyes to form brow ridges, defining their path points relative to the skull's ellipsoid center.

Placing the eye at roughly z1.30, y1.81 on the skull sphere, with the brow sitting .06 above it—though the eye decal height overlaps the brow line, which should be fine since the texture itself draws that detail. I'll shrink the eye to .055x.075 and set elevation to 0, then move on to the muzzle at z1.28.

Actually the muzzle and eye overlap at x.085 since the muzzle's half-width at its base reaches that far forward—I need to narrow the muzzle's starting station to .13 and push the stations further forward: adjusting the three muzzle cross-sections with new width/height values and positions. I'll also widen the skull radius and shift the eye azimuth to 55 degrees to clear the muzzle.

Recalculating with azimuth 58 degrees gives an eye position around x.106, z1.28, while the muzzle's half-width there is only .065, so they finally clear each other. I'm now setting the overall head proportions—skull length plus muzzle totaling about .5 for a lion-dragon look—and placing the antler bases at the top of the skull, then positioning nostril spheres and a nose pad with appropriate scaling, before starting on the upper fang spikes at the muzzle base.

Adding the lower fangs pointing upward from the jaw so they overlap properly with the upper ones, then sketching a dark seam along the muzzle's upper edge to define the mouth line, before moving on to plan the ear placement and orientation off the back of the head.

Defining the ear outline points...

Now sketching the antler geometry — base joints, beam path points curving up and back with tapering radii, and color bands along the sweep for the gold and ivory tones.

Still shaping antler tines...

Adding gem placement...

Now I'm checking the neck and head joint positions to make sure the mane frame builds correctly off the neck segment before the jewelry gets attached.

Still working out body sweep radii...

Checking the thigh bulge protrudes nicely past the body outline as a haunch, and confirming the fore leg root position lines up with its target. Now I'm defining the leg coloring logic, shading cream fur near the hoof, gold coat above that, and the base coat color higher up the leg.

Skipping gold bracers at the knee since hind hock heights vary too much to pin down consistently. I'm resolving how to grab the hoof's final joint safely in TypeScript, falling back to the last joint in the chain if the tip is missing, then sketching out a helper function to build each leg with named joints like shoulder and elbow for front versus hind variants.

Working out the radius tapering arrays for fore and hind leg tubes, with hind thighs starting thicker at the hip to account for the haunch, and placing the hoof cylinders slightly offset and stretched along the z-axis for a more natural foot shape.

I'm sketching out the facial details now too — skipping claws and belly plating for simplicity, but adding a jaw beard using a tapering curved path with gold coloring, plus considering a tassel pendant element hanging from the collar as a gold cord accessory.

For the tassels, I'm figuring out how to place card frames along a curve at the collar front, positioning a few strands near the midpoint of that loop with narrow texture cards for the dangling strands. Then I'm thinking about adding a jade disc pendant using a flat cylinder shape oriented along the y-axis at that attachment point.

For the pendant placement, I need to compute an outward offset from the neck curve toward the underside-front direction, using the loop's tangent to figure out which way is "closest to up" so the disc hangs naturally at the right angle.

I'm sweeping the gold collar loop along its path, planning two loops at slightly different parameters and radii for a chunkier band and a thinner one, and considering skipping a chest medallion decal to keep things simple.

For the legs, I'm scattering cloud-puff cards near the knees using a seeded random generator, applying a glow effect to those card meshes, and setting up a texture decal for the eyes. I'm also tuning sweep segment counts for small tubes to keep the overall part count moderate.

Now I'm sketching out the actual file: setting up imports for THREE, the builder utilities, frame, limb/IK helpers, and the paint/scales/gradient modules needed for coloring the body and legs, then starting to write the import statements concretely.

Writing import statements...

I'm also mapping out the color palette, making sure every constant gets used since unused ones trigger errors, and planning to keep the flat-string colors like teal and gold minimal while routing most hues through the paint system.

Still defining scale patterns and fur coat colors...

I'm now sketching out the leg paint logic with layered color bands, then moving into SVG texture definitions for cloud-like plume shapes using stacked circles of varying sizes.

Still writing SVG code...

I should type the circle arrays as explicit tuples to avoid TypeScript inference issues, then move on to designing a swirl-shaped puff cloud for the 64x64 variant using a similar cluster of overlapping circles.

Now I'm sketching a flame shape and a decorative gold swirl made of concentric arcs for a flank decal, checking that the arc path segments connect smoothly at each joint.

Writing the tassel cord and knot shape...

Setting up the root joint orientation, then building the spine chain with a catmull-rom curve through a few points along the back, and starting the tail chain similarly.

Adding tail curve points, then defining the neck chain attached to the third spine joint using another catmull curve up toward the head position.

Still defining the body sweep... I need to fix the radius function's return type annotation so TypeScript accepts the tuple, then work out a tapering radius sequence for the neck sweep that connects smoothly where it meets the body.

Writing leg-building loop code...

I realize I need unique joint names to avoid clashes, so I'll use shoulder/elbow/wrist/hoofF for the front legs and hip/knee/hock/hoofH for the hind legs, parented to spine or hips respectively.

Now I'm adding muscle ellipsoids attached to the leg bones with coat shading, then building the hoof cylinder positioned at the foot tip with slight offsets for a natural stance.

Still writing hoof details... adding a gold cuff ring near the top and a dark cleft box on the front face, working out the positioning math so it sits flush against the hoof's tapered surface.

Now I'm figuring out the fetlock flame ring using evenly spaced items along the leg chain, then setting up elbow and hock card placement by scattering points across the leg's swept surface with filters for normal direction and height range so they land on the back of the leg in a believable spot.

For the hind legs I'm adjusting the y range since the hock sits lower than the elbow, settling on a shared range that works for both front and back. The plume cards get sized and angled to look like a tuft of cloud-like fur trailing off the leg.

Now I'm moving to the head, setting up the eye with a glowing iris color and placing decals by finding surface hit points mirrored left and right on the skull.

I'm defining the skull as a scaled, non-uniform sphere attached to the head bone, then lofting the muzzle shape from a series of width/height cross-sections running forward from the face.

Now I'm adding cheek and lip pad details as small spheres positioned along the muzzle, then starting the lower jaw loft shape...

Checking that the jaw's top edge touches the muzzle's bottom edge at matching z-stations so there's no gap, then adding a cream-colored belly tint under the jaw using normal-based shading. I'm starting to lay out whisker chains as point arrays along the muzzle.

I'm sweeping a tapered jaw curve with gold coloring for the beard shape, tapering radius down to a point at the chin. I'll skip adding tuft cards at the beard tip to avoid overcomplicating it, then move to placing cheek tufts by sampling points around the skull surface at specific angles.

Now I'm positioning puff cards for the forelock crest at several elevation angles above the head, plus side crests at an angle offset, sizing and leaning the plume cards for a swept-back look. Ears and antlers follow the earlier plan, and the gold circlet jewel is already placed. For dorsal spikes I'm deciding to skip the spine ridge since the mane already covers that area, and I'm starting to write code for body decal placement along the torso surface, mirrored on both sides.

I'm realizing the hind swirl decal overlaps the haunch sphere and gets hidden behind it, so I need to reposition it higher and forward to stay visible, and similarly nudge the shoulder swirl to avoid the muscle bulge -- repositioning the swirl decals to keep them visible on the body surface.

I'm extending this to a generic haunches array so I can apply the same swirl/shoulder decal logic across parts, skipping extras like a jade medallion or chest plate for now. Then I'm building the collar by generating a loop surface around the neck and sweeping gold geometry along it.

Adding second collar band...

For the pendant, I'm placing a jewel offset below the collar's midpoint and starting to define its jade cylinder geometry.

Now I'm placing frames along the tail for cloud-streamer cards, looping across angles and t-values, with thinner plume/flame cards clustered near the tip to taper it off.

Then I'm adding withers and chest tufts using sparser angle ranges off the body spine, and neck plumes starting lower, mixing plume and flame variants for texture.

Checking the mane stays dorsal without drifting to the front of the neck, confirming t-semantics for neck sampling, and auditing unused imports to make sure everything like bezier, catmull, ink shading, gradients, and glow helpers are actually in use.

Now I'm building the antler joint, computing a Catmull-Rom beam for each tine and placing a joint at its base with directional orientation, naming it antlerL or antlerR based on side. I'm sweeping the beam into a tapered ivory-colored antler shape with banding...

Checking that the antler base sits right at the skull surface geometrically, I adjust the y-position slightly to ensure the base radius touches the skull without floating or clipping.

Now I'm adding a small collar torus near the base of the antler beam to visually anchor it, sized smaller than the beam tube so it wraps snugly. Then I move to building the tine branches, iterating over a few points along the beam to compute tip positions that angle outward and upward from each branch point.

Writing bezier sweep code...

Defining more frame types...

I'm working out ring item defaults and part counts, then moving to the glow effect for the flame emissive texture.

Now I'm adding detail passes for teeth and mouth, setting up whisker chains with tapered radius and gold coloring, and building the ear joint parts with vector calculations.

Adding the inner ear outline...

Tracing out the ridge curve points along the muzzle, checking each station's height against the skull and muzzle cross-sections to make sure the gold stripe sits just above the surface consistently from the skull down to the nose tip.

With the brow ridges settled, I'm skipping cheek decals and checking the flank swirl decal placement against the body surface, then writing a helper that filters out null hits when sampling points around the skull for the forelock cards, using a type guard to narrow the array to non-null hits.

Now I'm verifying build order—torso sweeps need to come before the leg scatter since legs use their own sweep chain, and double-checking that sweep radii arrays have enough keys for smooth interpolation. I'm also setting up the haunch parts structure to track part, surface, and kind together.

Checking the mouth seam placement against the muzzle geometry — the seam curve's width and position seem to land below the muzzle bottom, closer to the jaw line than the muzzle surface itself, so I need to verify the coordinates align properly.

I'll skip the mouth seam entirely since nostrils and fangs give enough facial detail without it. For nostrils, I'm placing small ink-colored spheres embedded into the nose pad near the front of the muzzle, positioned symmetrically on either side. The nose pad itself is a flattened sphere shape sitting at the muzzle front. With that settled, I'm ready to write the final part code attaching these pieces to the head bone.

Now I'm sorting out the limb joint arguments—root position as a number array and bend points as nested arrays—plus the hoof placement and a ring positioned partway along the leg. The sweep chain should work fine with default naming, so I'll write out the file carefully, watching the template string syntax.
